title: A human checked support inbox loop
promise: Sort incoming questions and prepare reply drafts for a person to review.
whatItIs: n8n is a workflow builder that connects services and can include AI steps. A small student version could take incoming support messages, label them by topic, and prepare a draft reply for review. A workflow is a set of connected steps that runs when an event occurs.
whoPays: Hypothesis: a small online shop with a recurring support inbox might pay for setup or maintenance; the supplied page does not establish demand for this student service.
loop: A new test support email triggers the workflow.
Rules remove obvious junk and pass the message to a classifier.
The classifier assigns a topic and priority.
The workflow retrieves an approved answer note and drafts a reply.
A person reviews and sends the draft, correcting uncertain cases.
The workflow records the outcome for later review.
evidence: The n8n page describes integrations, AI workflows, templates, human approvals and execution monitoring. It attributes to SanctifAI a first workflow setup in two hours; this is a vendor-published case study, not independent verification. The source shows an automation platform, not this proposed inbox service or its earnings.
uncertainty: This is a proposed small version, not a claim that n8n autonomously runs a support business. Email permissions, model costs, privacy, errors and integration setup need testing. A person must approve customer-facing replies and handle unusual or sensitive messages. The page does not prove demand for this offer.
first24Hours: Choose a test inbox and write ten fictional support messages.
Build a workflow that labels those messages and drafts replies from a short approved FAQ.
Run the examples, record misclassifications, and add a human approval step before any send action.

ease.reason: A narrow visual workflow can be configured from templates and integrations; live service setup still needs technical work.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a small support team may pay for inbox triage; the source establishes no demand for this student offer.

feasibility.reason: One inbox demo can fit two weeks; production integrations, reliability and onboarding remain substantial limits.

autonomy.reason: Triggers can label and draft repeatedly; a person must review replies and handle errors, consistent with the page’s human checkpoints.

evidence.reason: The first-party page documents a working platform and attributes a two-hour setup to one case study, not independent use evidence.
